sections.section_name: Section B - Very Short Analytical Concepts

questions.question_text: Define Body Mass Index (BMI) and state its primary utility in health and fitness assessments. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Body Mass Index is a statistical ratio of a person's weight to their height. It is primarily used as a screening tool to categorize individuals into healthy, underweight, overweight, or obese matrices.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between health-related physical fitness and skill-related physical fitness matrices. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Health-related fitness focuses on overall systemic wellness and disease prevention (e.g., strength, flexibility). Skill-related fitness targets performance-enhancing attributes required for competitive sports, such as agility, speed, and reaction time.

questions.question_text: Briefly outline two fundamental safety guidelines that must be followed before commencing river rafting. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Participants must wear certified personal flotation devices (life jackets) at all times and undergo a comprehensive briefing on navigating rapids and responding to capsize emergencies.

questions.question_text: Explain the concept of 'Seeding' in the engineering of tournament fixtures. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Seeding is an administrative procedure where top-ranking or highly skilled teams are strategically placed in separate brackets of a fixture to prevent them from eliminating each other in the initial rounds.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of executing a proper first aid protocol immediately after a sports injury? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The primary purpose is to preserve the athlete's life, prevent the injury from deteriorating further, alleviate acute pain, and promote optimal conditions for long-term medical recovery.

sections.section_name: Section C - Short Explanatory & Anatomical Tiers

questions.question_text: Describe the procedural steps and physiological utility of the Sit and Reach test in evaluating physical fitness. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The athlete sits with legs fully extended and reaches forward along a measuring box without jerking. This test evaluates the flexibility of the lower back and hamstring muscles, which is vital for preventing musculoskeletal injuries and ensuring full structural mobility.

questions.question_text: Outline the essential safety equipment and environmental precautions strictly required when organizing a rock climbing adventure sport activity. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Essential gear includes UIAA-certified helmets, dynamic climbing ropes, secure harnesses, and chalk. Environmental precautions require checking weather forecasts to avoid slippery terrain, ensuring stable rock faces, and always climbing with a trained belayer securing the anchor system.

questions.question_text: Explain the administrative and competitive differences between Extramural and Intramural sporting competitions within an educational framework. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Intramural competitions are played strictly within the walls of an institution to promote mass participation and basic health. Extramural competitions involve specialized teams traveling to compete against other institutions, focusing on elite performance, school prestige, and advanced talent development.

questions.question_text: Detail the immediate management steps for a soft tissue injury like a severe ankle sprain using the standard R.I.C.E. protocol. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Rest the injured joint to prevent further tearing. Apply Ice to constrict blood vessels and reduce localized swelling. Compress the area with an elastic bandage for structural support, and Elevate the ankle above the heart to drain excess fluid.

questions.question_text: Discuss the physiological importance of measuring and tracking cardiorespiratory endurance for athletes participating in marathon running. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Cardiorespiratory endurance reflects the efficiency of the heart and lungs to supply oxygenated blood to working muscles. Tracking it allows marathon runners to optimize their aerobic threshold, delay the onset of lactic acid buildup, and sustain prolonged mechanical exertion.

questions.question_text: A physical education teacher conducts health matrices assessments. A 16-year-old student weighs 75 kg and is 1.6 meters tall. Calculate their exact Body Mass Index (BMI) and classify their weight category based on standard health matrices. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: BMI is calculated as weight divided by height squared: 75 / (1.6 * 1.6) = 75 / 2.56, which equals 29.3. According to standard BMI matrices, a score of 29.3 places the student directly into the 'Overweight' category, nearing the threshold for Class I Obesity.

questions.question_text: Read the following tournament data context: A sports coordinator draws up a competitive league framework for 13 participating teams using a standard Knockout Fixture layout. Compute the total number of matches required and determine the exact allocation of 'Byes' across the upper and lower halves of the draw. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Total matches required equals N - 1, which is 13 - 1 = 12 matches. The next highest power of two is 16, meaning total Byes = 16 - 13 = 3 Byes. The lower half receives (3 + 1) / 2 = 2 Byes, while the upper half receives 1 Bye.

questions.question_text: Analyze the specific physiological and psychological benefits of engaging in outdoor adventure sports, such as mountaineering and trekking, for school-going adolescents experiencing high academic stress. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Physiologically, trekking builds robust cardiovascular endurance and strengthens lower-body mechanics. Psychologically, navigating unpredictable natural environments forces adolescents to develop resilient problem-solving skills, significantly reduces cortisol-linked academic stress, and fosters deep emotional confidence through successful physical risk management.

sections.section_name: Section E - Long-Form Structural Rules & Training

questions.question_text: Elaborate on the complete structural procedure for drawing a knockout fixture for 21 teams. Explain the mathematical calculation of total matches, rounds, total byes, and the specific distribution of teams across the upper and lower halves. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: For 21 teams, total matches are 21 - 1 = 20. The next power of two is 32, requiring 32 - 21 = 11 Byes. Rounds equal 5 (since 2^5 = 32). Teams are split into halves: Upper half has (21 + 1)/2 = 11 teams, Lower half has 10 teams. Byes are distributed as 6 in the lower half and 5 in the upper half to balance the second round.

questions.question_text: Define physical fitness and comprehensively discuss its five major health-related components, highlighting how each specific component contributes to overall systemic wellness and injury prevention in daily life. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Physical fitness is the capacity to perform daily tasks without undue fatigue. Its five health-related components are: Cardiovascular Endurance (heart/lung efficiency), Muscular Strength (force exertion to prevent structural weakness), Muscular Endurance (sustained muscle activity), Flexibility (joint mobility to prevent tears), and Body Composition (lean-to-fat ratio to stave off metabolic disorders).

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the standard protocols and administrative responsibilities involved in organizing a large-scale school sports tournament. Detail the specific functions of the pre-tournament, during-tournament, and post-tournament committees to ensure structural safety and success. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Pre-tournament committees handle budget logistics, venue preparation, equipment safety checks, and sending invitations. During the tournament, technical and disciplinary committees ensure fair officiating, manage crowds, and execute rapid first aid protocols. Post-tournament committees are responsible for prize distribution, finalizing media reports, reconciling financial accounts, and securely storing institutional equipment.
